newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former House speaker Uthai Pimchaichon has been elected president of the Constitution Drafting Assembly, beating another strong candidate, Anand Panyarachun, who is now being backed to lead the drafting process. Uthai says the new constitution must be equipped with measures to maintain the prime minister's leadership, give him decision-making powers and enable him to appoint an able and efficient cabinet. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yubamrung has been given the task of going after value-added tax cheats. Chalerm says he is ready to take the assignment, but wants a clear government order or cabinet resolution giving him a mandate to arrest the culprits. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Food and Drug Administration plans to conduct chemical finger-printing of amphetamine-like stimulants in order to get to the source of illegal production of controlled substances being widely used in the country. Narcotics Control Division official says chemical finger-printing will enable the Administration to identify the exact chemical compounds and put the authorities within reach of their production base. (BANGKOK POST)

- State agencies today begin looking at ways to prune public spending by at least 100 billion baht and set investment priorities for the next five years. The cabinet called for the step yesterday to ensure a balanced budget in the 1997 and 1998 fiscal years. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Senior officials of the Finance Ministry, Bank of Thailand, Government Housing Bank and the Government Savings Bank are to meet today to find measures to assist the troubled property developing business. It is expected that the Government Savings Bank will be asked to join a funding scheme which will be set up at the amount of 50.4 billion baht to help the business. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- The Bank of Thailand may provide the Bangkok Bank of Commerce with interest-free loans of not more than 60 billion baht instead of underwriting its non-performing loans to help it back into the black. The loan will be allocated to the bank in phases, with the first being a relatively large amount. (BUSINESS DAY)
